object_description: isolated non-aligned volumes like farmhouses, with the school stacked over a partly buried gym
geometry_property: unoccupied hall roof used as courtyard
design_condition: the volumes are placed like farmhouses, isolated and non-aligned, concentrated on the south-eastern side of the stream away from the road, with the school stacked over the buried gym and its roof used as a raised courtyard

positive: The project respects the typological village structure with isolated, non-aligned volumes
The spaces resulting from this composition define the accesses and exterior surfaces
The composition concentrates away from the nuisances of the main road
A public pedestrian connection is proposed, separate from the parking
It widens at the stream level to give access to the public functions
The gymnasium is partially buried and benefits from natural light on its east facade
Through a game of superposition the school sits above the gymnasium
The unoccupied roof area of the sports programme is used as a courtyard
The scale of the composition avoids the notion of a large school complex
The desired compactness allows land savings
The raised courtyard has a private character and is the central reference space of the school
The classroom building is organised in modules of four classes
A central and airy circulation distributes the modules generously and allows appropriation by users
This circulation is lit in second daylight from the rooms and by overhead light
All common functions and the main entrances overlook these outdoor spaces
negative: The fragmentation generates complicated basement circulation without natural light
This is not very obvious for students of the intended age group
The location of the service premises is questioned
There is a lack of space for changing rooms, benches and coat hooks
